description: Service-specific network traffic: Elasticsearch (9200/9300), Grafana (3000), Fleet Server (8220), and comprehensive ICMP monitoring with type/code/version/direction analysis.

panels.title: ES Traffic
panels.description:
Total bytes to Elasticsearch ports (9200 HTTP + 9300 transport). Primary cluster communication.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

targets.query: data_stream.dataset:network_traffic.flow AND host.name:($nt_host) AND (destination.port:9200 OR destination.port:9300)

panels.title: Grafana Traffic
panels.description:
Total bytes to Grafana (port 3000). Dashboard and API access.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

panels.title: Fleet Traffic
panels.description:
Total bytes to Fleet Server (port 8220). Agent checkin and policy distribution.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

panels.title: Other Traffic
panels.description:
Total bytes to ports other than ES, Grafana, and Fleet. Background services and OS traffic.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

targets.query: data_stream.dataset:network_traffic.flow AND host.name:($nt_host) AND NOT (destination.port:9200 OR destination.port:9300 OR destination.port:3000 OR destination.port:8220)

panels.title: ES HTTP (9200) by Source
panels.description:
Elasticsearch HTTP API traffic split by source IP. Shows which clients query ES most.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

panels.title: ES Transport (9300) by Source
panels.description:
Elasticsearch inter-node transport traffic by source. Dominated by cluster replication and shard movement.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

panels.title: Grafana Traffic Over Time
panels.description:
Grafana port 3000 bandwidth over time. Spikes correlate with dashboard rendering or API calls.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

panels.title: Fleet Server Traffic
panels.description:
Fleet Server port 8220 bandwidth over time. Regular pattern from agent checkin intervals.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.flow

panels.title: ICMP Packets Over Time
panels.description:
ICMP packet count over time. Includes ping monitoring, router solicitation, and unreachable notifications.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP by Source
panels.description:
ICMP packets split by source IP. Identifies which hosts are generating ICMP traffic.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP Type Breakdown
panels.description:
ICMP message types: RouterSolicitation (IPv6 NDP), DestinationUnreachable (port closed), NeighborSolicitation. Type distribution reveals network behavior.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP by Destination
panels.description:
ICMP packets split by destination IP. Shows what's being pinged or generating unreachable responses.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP Direction
panels.description:
ICMP traffic direction (ingress/egress). Our environment sees primarily ingress ICMP (responses to outbound connections).
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP Payload Size
panels.description:
Total ICMP payload bytes over time. Large ICMP payloads may indicate ICMP tunneling for data exfiltration.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP Version (v4/v6)
panels.description:
ICMP version split: ICMPv4 (ping, unreachable) vs ICMPv6 (NDP, router solicitation). IPv6 NDP is normal on dual-stack networks.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP Code Distribution
panels.description:
ICMP code values within each type. For DestinationUnreachable: code 3=port, code 1=host, code 0=network.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp

panels.title: ICMP Raw Log
panels.description:
Raw ICMP documents with source, destination, message type, type/code numbers, version, bytes, and direction.
Source: Network Traffic integration → network_traffic.icmp
